column5: remove a channel (you type its name to confirm): hs notify channel remove <name> [--yes]
column6: einen Kanal entfernen (zur Bestätigung den Namen tippen): hs notify channel remove <Name> [--yes]

column5: send one test message to one channel, whatever its minimum priority and the quiet hours: hs notify channel test <name>
column6: eine Testnachricht an einen Kanal schicken, gleich welche kleinste Priorität und Ruhezeit: hs notify channel test <Name>

column5: write the channels derived from notifyUrl and notifyUrlSecond as files (the first change does this by itself; nothing is lost)
column6: die aus notifyUrl und notifyUrlSecond abgeleiteten Kanäle als Dateien schreiben (die erste Änderung macht das von selbst; nichts geht verloren)

column5: the providers a channel can use and the settings of each
column6: die Anbieter, die ein Kanal nutzen kann, und deren Einstellungen

column5: the processor and the board's sensors: cpu-model, cpu-cores, cpu-threads, temp and fan rows (read only, no root)
the encrypted volumes of this server: type (vault|luks|zfs), device, state (open|locked|unmanaged), size (tab separated; other people's disks are not listed)
the vault's state, device, size, used and free bytes, age of the header backup (key and value lines)
who uses each vault item: name, text (tab separated)
shut the server down (asks first, waits while a backup, sync or pool change runs; --force, --dry-run)
column6: den Server herunterfahren (fragt vorher, wartet, solange Backup, Sync oder Pooländerung läuft; --force, --dry-run)

column5: reboot the server: hs reboot [--menu | --firmware | --entry <id>] (boot menu once, BIOS setup, or one boot entry once)
column6: den Server neu starten: hs reboot [--menu | --firmware | --entry <id>] (einmal das Boot-Menü, das BIOS-Setup oder ein Boot-Eintrag)

column5: shares given to other homeservers and shares mounted from them (state of each mount)
column6: Freigaben an andere Homeserver und von ihnen eingebundene Freigaben (Zustand jeder Einbindung)

column5: give another homeserver read access to a share: hs remote offer <share> --peer <name> (makes the login remote-<name>, prints what the other side types)
column6: einem anderen Homeserver Lesezugriff auf eine Freigabe geben: hs remote offer <Freigabe> --peer <Name> (legt den Login remote-<Name> an, zeigt, was die Gegenseite eintippt)

column5: take that access away again: hs remote revoke <peer> [<share>] (deletes the login when no share is left)
column6: den Zugriff wieder entziehen: hs remote revoke <Name> [<Freigabe>] (löscht den Login, wenn keine Freigabe mehr übrig ist)

column5: mount a share of another homeserver read-only: hs remote add <peer> <host> <share> --user <login> [--domain <DOMAIN>] (asks the password)
column6: eine Freigabe eines anderen Homeservers nur lesend einbinden: hs remote add <Name> <Host> <Freigabe> --user <Login> [--domain <DOMÄNE>] (fragt das Passwort)

column5: stop using a peer's share: unmount it and forget the login: hs remote remove <peer> [<share>]
column6: die Freigabe eines anderen Homeservers nicht mehr nutzen: aushängen und den Login vergessen: hs remote remove <Name> [<Freigabe>]

column5: give an instance the mounted shares of a peer, read only (e.g. for Jellyfin): hs remote attach <peer> <instance> [--path /media-<peer>]
column6: einer Instanz die eingebundenen Freigaben eines anderen Homeservers nur lesend geben (z. B. für Jellyfin): hs remote attach <Name> <Instanz> [--path /media-<Name>]

column5: take them away from the instance again: hs remote detach <peer> <instance>
column6: sie der Instanz wieder wegnehmen: hs remote detach <Name> <Instanz>

column5: offers and mounts, tab separated: kind, peer, share, host or login, state
mount what is set up and not mounted (the timer hs-remote-mount)
the UPS as key and value lines (state, charge, runtime, load), no root
column6: die USV als Schlüssel-Wert-Zeilen (Zustand, Ladung, Laufzeit, Last), ohne root

column5: things that run out on a date (certificate, token, domain, credentials), with the days left
column6: Dinge, die an einem Datum ablaufen (Zertifikat, Token, Domain, Zugangsdaten), mit den Tagen, die noch bleiben

column5: write down something that expires: hs expiry add <name> <YYYY-MM-DD> [how to renew]; the health check warns 30 and 7 days before
column6: Etwas eintragen, das abläuft: hs expiry add <Name> <JJJJ-MM-TT> [wie man es erneuert]; der Health-Check warnt 30 und 7 Tage vorher

column5: take an entry off the list: hs expiry remove <name>
column6: einen Eintrag von der Liste nehmen: hs expiry remove <Name>

column5: entries as name, date, days left, state (ok|soon|due|expired|invalid), how to renew
what adding or removing an expiry entry would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 2 = the date is missing)
do it (hs sys expiry start add <name> --date YYYY-MM-DD [--renew <text>] | remove <name>), answers status done
what running a recipe would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused, also for a recipe that needs something typed)
run a recipe as a background job with the stored answers or the defaults (hs sys recipes start <recipe> run [--name <container>]), answers status started and the unit

what applying the service routes to the reverse proxy, adopting hand-made routes, importing services or removing one would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused or nothing to do)
do it (hs sys routes start apply --confirm apply | adopt | import | remove <service>); apply is a background job, the others answer status done
what mounting a share of another homeserver, stopping it, taking back the access given, or attaching it to an instance would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused)

do it (hs sys peers start add <peer> <host> <share> --user <login> with the password on stdin | remove|revoke <peer> [<share>] --confirm <peer> | attach <peer> <instance> | detach <peer> <instance>), answers status done
what a header backup of the vault, moving secrets into it, closing it or fixing the permissions of the secrets would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused)
do it as a background job (hs sys secrets start header-backup | move [<name>] | close --confirm close | secrets-fix), answers status started and the unit
the questions a recipe wants answered before it runs, as data: key, label, kind (text|secret|choice:a,b), default, pattern, when (- when empty); the last row is input and form|terminal|none
what a test push message, pinning the MACs, moving the upload cache or cleaning the fans would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused)
do it (hs sys admin start test-push | pin-macs | cache-mover | fans-clean [--seconds N]); the first two answer done, the others start a job
files whose name contains a word, in every snapshot, as data: snapshot, time, path, type, bytes (at most 200; mounts the backup disk, can take a while)
the CA of this setup and the certificate of the domain controller as key and value lines: ca, ca_until, dc, cert, subject, names, valid_until, days_left, checked
what making the CA or renewing the certificate of the domain controller would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused)
do it (hs sys dc start ca | renew [--dc <instance>] --confirm <instance>); ca answers done, renew starts a job
what connecting the router would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; the API key is the first line on standard input; exit 0 ok, 1 refused, 2 = address or key missing)
do it (hs sys net start setup --address <url>, the API key on standard input), answers status done
what the collector keeps for the web interface, oldest first: read, age in seconds, milliseconds it took, exit code, bytes (which reads are slow, which are stale)
keep the output of a read (standard input) in the state database; only the collector (reads-collect.sh) calls it
the output the collector kept for a read (exit 1: none)
every read the collector keeps, as data: read, interval in seconds, age of the kept output (-1 = never), milliseconds, exit code, bytes
ask the live-state collector to read these topics again now (--all: every topic); returns at once
every live-state topic: topic, interval, age in seconds (-1 = none), generation, exit code, error, error time
problems of the live state (Redis down, a topic older than three intervals): key and text
read the slow reads of the web interface and keep their output in the state database (the timer hs-reads-collect does it every 15 s; --all ignores the intervals)
extension packages as name, on|off, commands, nix (yes = a rebuild switches it), title
list the packages (recipes and extensions) with their version: hs pkg list [--all] [--kind recipe|extension]
column6: die Pakete (Rezepte und Erweiterungen) mit Version auflisten: hs pkg list [--all] [--kind recipe|extension]

column5: the packages whose version in the tree is newer than the one last applied
column6: die Pakete, deren Version im Baum neuer ist als die zuletzt angewendete

column5: check every package manifest
column6: alle Paket-Manifeste prüfen

column5: every package as data: name, kind, version, applied version (- = never), audience, title
update the package repositories and find the newest verified release
column6: die Paket-Repositories aktualisieren und das neueste geprüfte Release finden

column5: what the package repositories offer (after hs pkg fetch)
column6: was die Paket-Repositories anbieten (nach hs pkg fetch)

column5: install a package from a repository (signed release, read-only copy): hs pkg install <name> [--repo <repo>]
column6: ein Paket aus einem Repository installieren (signiertes Release, schreibgeschützte Kopie): hs pkg install <Name> [--repo <Repo>]

column5: show what changed in a package, then install its new release: hs pkg update <name> [--yes]
column6: zeigen, was sich in einem Paket geändert hat, dann das neue Release installieren: hs pkg update <Name> [--yes]

column5: forget a package installed from a repository (a recipe's container stays)
column6: ein aus einem Repository installiertes Paket vergessen (der Container eines Rezepts bleibt)

column5: the package repositories: the two defaults and the ones that were added
column6: die Paket-Repositories: die beiden Standard-Repositories und die hinzugefügten

column5: add a package repository (releases must be signed): hs pkg repo add <name> <url> --key <allowed_signers file>
column6: ein Paket-Repository hinzufügen (Releases müssen signiert sein): hs pkg repo add <Name> <URL> --key <allowed_signers-Datei>

column5: remove a repository that was added
column6: ein hinzugefügtes Repository entfernen

column5: what the repositories offer as data: repo, package, kind, version, applied version (- = not installed)
every installable package as data: name, kind, repo, available version, installed version (- = none), state (new|current|update|orphan), core (yes|no), audience, title
the package repositories as data: name, address, signed|unsigned, default|added
what installing, updating or removing a package, fetching, or adding or removing a repository would do, as data: status, plan lines (never asks; exit 0 ok, 1 refused)
do it (hs sys pkg start install <name> [--repo R] | update <name> | remove <name> | fetch [<repo>] | repo-add <name> <url> (key line on stdin) | repo-remove <name>); red changes need --confirm <name>
